To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Davies-Bouldin index is the best index for most cases, (2) the Davies-Boudin index is not always the best index, (3) the Calinski-Harabasz index is the best for datasets that are well separated and have many samples, (4) the Silhouette index is the best when the dataset is noisy and the number of samples is low, (5) the Dunn index is the best in the presence of outliers, (6)
the Silhouette index is the best overall index, but the Davies-Bouldin index is the best for most of the applications.

(i) there is not a single best validity index that outperforms all other indices in all possible situations, (ii) the best indices are different for different clustering algorithms and (iii) there are indices that perform better in some situations than other indices, even if they are not the best ones overall.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions.
the following questions: What are the most appropriate cluster validity indices for different clustering problems?
the following questions: Which index is the most suitable for each environment?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are no best indices, only indices that work better in certain circumstances than others.
there is no single index that is superior in every situation.
there is not a single best index for all situations and, in fact, the choice of an index should depend on the specific problem to be solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no best index and the choice of a suitable index depends on the characteristics of the dataset and of the application.
the Davies-Bouldin (DB) index is the best index to use in general.
the Davies-Bouldin index and the silhouette width are the best indices in general, while the Xie-Beni index and the Dunn index are the best for the case of well separated clusters.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of the different indices is strongly dependent on the data characteristics.
there is no universal index that can be used for any application.
there is no single best index.
